newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gle Eaux head not ruling out any options on CGV.
newsitem.headline: Gle Eaux head not ruling out any options on CGV.

text.p: Jean-Marie Messier, chairman of France's Compagnie Generale des Eaux (CGE) said on Friday he did not rule out any options in the sale of cable unit Compagnie Generale de Videcommunication (CGV).
"I do not rule out anything. When one gets offers, one looks at them," Messier told Reuters on the sideline of the annual shareholders' meeting of Canal Plus.

CGE currently owns 70 percent of CGV. But recent press reports have said CGE could cut its stake to 20 percent, while Canal Plus would raise its holding to 35 from 20 percent and Time Warner would step in to acquire a 35 percent interest. The balance would be held by financial investors, including Societe Generale, which already controls eight percent of CGV.

Under an agreement between media group Havas and CGE, CGE became the largest shareholder in Havas and Havas the major shareholder in Canal Plus. At the time of the deal CGE said it wanted to sell CGV.
